accuracy.evidence: Checked against NC 2013 Y2 Living things and their habitats (identify that most living things live in habitats to which they are suited, including micro-habitats) and the RSPB / Field Studies Council woodlouse notes: woodlice are terrestrial crustaceans that lose water through the cuticle and breathe with pleopod lungs that must stay moist, so they shelter in damp, dark places by day; earthworms respire through moist skin; slugs and snails forage at night and in wet weather; pond skaters walk on the water surface film; butterflies bask in sun and feed on nectar. The 7 of 8 choice-chamber result is shown as 'most', with one woodlouse left behind, matching real classroom results rather than a perfect 8 of 8.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets documented early-years ideas (Nuffield Primary SPACE 'Variety of life'; ASE Primary Science on choice chambers): animals live somewhere by chance or near people (match step feedback for every wrong home), all animals in a test behave the same (one woodlouse stays dry; mastery m5 on Mia's one-woodlouse claim; challenge 'even'), woodlice like the light so they can see (step 2 prediction), habitats are fixed places rather than conditions (weather detective: slugs hide under stones on a hot afternoon but come onto the lawn in the rain), and pond snail vs garden snail confusion (snail|log feedback).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagmbhab is a choice-chamber and conditions lab: tap half a tray to wet it and watch woodlice gather on the damp side, repeat with bark for dark v light, match four minibeasts to soil, log, sunny flower and pond, watch a woodlouse's body-water meter fall on a sunny path and carry it back, then track slugs, bees and pond skaters as the weather changes. flagbug is about what a minibeast is (backbone sort, legs with a hand lens); flaganwhere places animals on land, water and air and continents. Max 6-shingle similarity 5.5% (flag_bgraph.js).

lab_teaches.evidence: The child chooses which half to wet or cover and the woodlice move only after Wait, so the preference is seen, not told; the two trays separate damp from dark as two different conditions; the water meter dropping to 35% on the path and refilling under the log shows why they hide; the weather rounds make the child change the answer for the same slug when the day turns rainy, so 'habitat suits conditions' is discovered.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions with tempting wrong options disproved on screen: 'the dry side' or 'half and half' (7 of 8 crawl to the damp side), 'the light side, so they can see' (7 of 8 go under the bark), and 'they like to swim' / 'scared of birds only' for why woodlice hide (the water meter shows drying out).

challenge_feedback.evidence: slip() has eight distinct messages (dry, even, sunny, water, myth, dark, under, land), each naming the slip and the fix, e.g. 'They do not spread out. In the tray, 7 of 8 went to the damp side.' In-lab wrong homes get twelve pair-specific messages (e.g. worm under the log: 'Worms do visit logs, but they spend most of their life deep in the soil'), and each wrong weather spot explains what the minibeast needs right now.

readability.evidence: validate_lessons passes for the family audience: kid FK 1.2, adult FK 8.7. Lab text uses short words (damp, dry, dark, sunny, home) for ages 5 to 7; the class 'young' gives 56 px buttons and larger step text.

no_filler.evidence: Content gate passes (no banned phrases; explanation overlap 1.0% with Where animals live, under 12% with all lessons). Kid paragraphs: what a micro-habitat is; conditions; who likes what; weather changes. Adult paragraphs: curriculum and key words; named mistakes; the biology of why; what the lab does.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots after Show me on every step at 360 px Android in light and dark and on iPhone 13. First pass placed the starting woodlice in a diagonal line, drew the minibeast icons too small in the cards, and wrote 'Damp log' and 'Sunny path' in a fixed dark ink that vanished on the dark theme, and woodlice under the bark were dark on dark; fixed with a 2-column start grid, bigger icons, theme text colour for the captions and pale woodlice on the dark half. Tray halves, home boxes and spot boxes are over 100 px tall.

accessibility.evidence: Every drag has buttons ('Make the left side damp', 'Cover the right side with bark', 'Wait and watch the woodlice', 'Put the worm in the soil', 'Move the woodlouse to the sunny path', 'Look under a stone'). say() updates the canvas aria-label and narration after each action, including the count and the water level. walk.cjs: desktop and iPhone 13 complete all 5 tasks with Show me, the challenge shows, axe WCAG 2.1 AA clean in both themes, no console errors.
